text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgarian chief prosecutor's office has issued detention orders for bankers from commercial banks put in receivership by the central bank and some of them are expected to be arrested before the ruling Socialist party congress during the weekend, the newspaper said without quoting sources. @

-- The shareholders of Bulgaria's private St Nikola International Orthodox Bank raised its capital to 2.2 billion levs from 800 million levs and agreed to sell a majority stake to the Bulgarian branch of Russia's oil producer Yukos Petroleum.

-- The central bank (BNB) board would probably be responsible for the implementation of a currency board system in Bulgaria which was the reason why the opposition demanded the resignation of current board members, which it sees as dominated by the ruling Socialists.

-- The BNB rejected a report by the private Seven Days radio station that it had discussed on Friday putting state-owned United Bulgarian Bank and Post Bank in receivership and filing a bankruptcy suit against state Biohim bank.

-- The government discussed the 1997 budget draft at a night session on Monday. An exchange rate of 400 levs per dollar and 40 percent cumulative annual inflation were assumed in the draft in case a currency board system was introduced in the country.

-- Bulgarian State Railway experts are expected to discuss with their Russian counterparts in Moscow conclusion of direct contracts between the two state railway companies in a bid to cut sharply cargo tariffs between the two countries.
-- Prices of government monitored basic goods rose by 10.9 percent in the past 15 days, the National Statistics Institute said.
-- Bulgarians are spending 46 percent of their income for food, a study by trade unions' Institute for Social Research showed, institute's director Rumyana Kraleva said.
